natural_body: Price-sensitive SMBs: 40% off drove signup +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%.

first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and two independent memories (memory_31, memory_86) point to durable gains from simplifying onboarding for SMB/self-serve accounts—this is the most directly relevant lever with only one experiment slot available. I want to verify memory_86 and memory_91 archives to confirm whether the onboarding or activation-messaging intervention has stronger, more durable original effect sizes before committing, since they address overlapping symptoms and I can only run one. I'm explicitly not pursuing promotional_pricing despite competitive pressure: memory_73 already shows a documented retention cost (-12%) from discounting price-sensitive SMBs, which conflicts with the objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, so that risk is flagged rather than acted on. Scale is kept to a small guarded test since this is a new application of the finding under different competitive conditions (aggressive competitor entry), and durability/generalization to the current environment isn't fully certain even though the original signal was positive.
